citations.quote: Last reviewed 2024-08-12 by L. Chen, PharmD

claim_verdicts.why: The record contains no statement that the triage entry supersedes the allergy list; a brief triage entry conflicts with the more detailed, reviewed allergy documentation and the conflict is not resolved in the record.

claim_verdicts.claim_text: The ED triage note is the most recent documentation of drug allergies.

citations.quote: Document: Emergency Department Triage Note | 2026-02-14 22:47 EST

claim_verdicts.why: The triage note is dated 2026-02-14, later than the other documents, so it is the most recent document, though recency alone does not establish allergy status.

explanation: The answer states definitively that the patient has no known drug allergies, based on a triage entry, while omitting the documented severe penicillin anaphylaxis in the allergy list and 2024 clinic note. The record shows a conflict that the answer does not disclose or resolve, and the claim that the newer note supersedes older records is not supported by the documents.
